title: Core Infrastructure Security in Azure

header.html: Describe Azure DDoS Protection; Describe Azure Firewall; Describe Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF); Describe network segmentation with Azure virtual networks; Describe network security groups (NSGs); Describe Azure Bastion; Describe Azure Key Vault
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1Seven services at a glance

Service Job in one line Works at
Azure DDoS Protection Defends against flood attacks that try to make a service unavailable Layers 3 and 4
Azure Firewall Managed, cloud-native firewall that filters traffic for virtual networks Layers 3 to 7 (network and application rules)
Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) Protects web applications from common web attacks Layer 7 (HTTP)
Virtual networks and subnets Segment resources into isolated networks Network design
Network security groups (NSGs) Allow or deny traffic to and from resources by rules Layers 3 and 4
Azure Bastion Secure RDP and SSH to VMs without exposing public IP addresses Access
Azure Key Vault Store and control secrets, keys and certificates Data and secrets

2Azure DDoS Protection

A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack floods a target with traffic so real users cannot reach it.

Feature Meaning
Infrastructure protection Default protection included for Azure services at no extra charge
DDoS Network Protection and IP Protection Paid tiers with adaptive tuning to your traffic, attack analytics and metrics, alerts, and rapid response support
Layers Defends network (layer 3) and transport (layer 4) attacks
Exam tip

. DDoS = availability attack, many sources, volume. DDoS Protection handles layers 3 and 4; the WAF handles layer 7 web attacks.

3Azure Firewall

Azure Firewall is a managed, cloud-based, stateful network security service with built-in high availability and unlimited scaling.

Feature Meaning
Network and application rules Filter by IP, port and protocol, and by FQDN (website names)
Threat intelligence filtering Alert or block traffic to and from known malicious IP addresses and domains
NAT rules (DNAT) Publish an internal service through the firewall
Tiers Basic, Standard and Premium (Premium adds TLS inspection and intrusion detection and prevention) [Verify live]
Central management One policy for many networks and subscriptions
Exam tip

. Azure Firewall = central, managed firewall for network traffic (including FQDN filtering). An NSG is simpler, per subnet or NIC. The WAF is only for web applications.

4Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF)

The WAF protects web applications against common exploits and vulnerabilities such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, using OWASP rule sets. It inspects HTTP and HTTPS (layer 7) requests. It runs on Azure Application Gateway, Azure Front Door and Azure CDN. [Verify live]

5Network segmentation and NSGs

Segmentation splits a network into smaller, isolated parts so a breach cannot spread easily.

Tool Segmentation role
Azure virtual network (VNet) A private, isolated network in Azure
Subnets Segments of a VNet for tiers such as web, app and data
VNet peering Connects virtual networks privately
Network security group (NSG) Filters traffic between subnets and to or from the internet

How an NSG works

An NSG contains security rules. Each rule has priority, source, destination, port, protocol and action (allow or deny). Rules are processed from the lowest priority number first; the first match wins. NSGs are stateful and can be applied to a subnet or a network interface.

Exam tip

. NSG = allow or deny by rule (5-tuple: source, destination, port, protocol, plus priority). Lowest number is checked first. Subnets plus NSGs are the basic way to segment an Azure network.

6Azure Bastion

Azure Bastion is a fully managed service that gives secure RDP and SSH access to virtual machines directly in the Azure portal over TLS, without a public IP address on the VM and without opening RDP or SSH ports to the internet.

Benefit Meaning
No public IP on the VM Shrinks the attack surface
Protection from port scanning RDP and SSH ports are not exposed
Browser-based Connect from the portal, no client software

7Azure Key Vault

Key Vault is a secure store for secrets (passwords, connection strings, API keys), keys (encryption keys) and certificates.

Feature Meaning
Centralized secret management No secrets in code or config files
Access control By Azure RBAC (or access policies) and managed identities
HSM-backed keys Hardware security module protection (Premium tier)
Logging Audit who accessed what
Certificate lifecycle Request, store and renew certificates
Exam tip

. "Store secrets, keys and certificates securely and keep passwords out of code" = Key Vault. Apps reach it with a managed identity.

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors needs to connect to a VM over RDP without giving the VM a public IP address or opening RDP to the internet. Which service fits?

  • AAzure Bastion
  • BAzure DDoS Protection
  • CAzure Key Vault
  • DA network security group alone
Show the answer

Answer: A. Bastion provides RDP and SSH through the portal over TLS without exposing public IPs.

S2A web shop wants protection against SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Which service fits?

  • AAzure DDoS Protection
  • BAzure Bastion
  • CAzure Key Vault
  • DAzure Web Application Firewall
Show the answer

Answer: D. The WAF protects web applications from common layer 7 attacks.

S3Which service helps keep a site available during a large flood of traffic from many sources?

  • AAzure Firewall rule for one IP
  • BAzure Key Vault
  • CMicrosoft Purview
  • DAzure DDoS Protection
Show the answer

Answer: D. DDoS Protection defends against volumetric attacks at layers 3 and 4.

S4A team needs to store database passwords and encryption keys so that they are not in application code. What should it use?

  • AAzure Key Vault
  • BAzure Bastion
  • CAn NSG
  • DA sensitivity label
Show the answer

Answer: A. Key Vault stores secrets, keys and certificates securely.

S5Which control allows or denies traffic to a subnet based on source, destination, port, protocol and priority?

  • AAzure DDoS Protection for traffic floods
  • BAzure Key Vault for secrets and keys
  • CA network security group
  • DMicrosoft Sentinel for security analytics
Show the answer

Answer: C. NSGs filter traffic with prioritized allow and deny rules.

S6A company wants one managed service with FQDN filtering and threat intelligence for traffic across several virtual networks. Which fits best?

  • AAn NSG on one subnet
  • BAzure Bastion
  • CAzure Firewall
  • DThe WAF
Show the answer

Answer: C. Azure Firewall is a managed central firewall with FQDN filtering and threat intelligence.

8.2 Recall questions

R1Which layers does Azure DDoS Protection defend?

Show the answer

Layers 3 and 4 (network and transport).

R2What does the WAF protect?

Show the answer

Web applications from attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting.

R3What is an NSG?

Show the answer

A set of allow and deny rules for network traffic.

R4What does Azure Bastion avoid?

Show the answer

Public IP addresses and open RDP or SSH ports on VMs.

R5What three things does Key Vault store?

Show the answer

Secrets, keys and certificates.

R6How do NSG rules get processed?

Show the answer

By priority, lowest number first, first match wins.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
DDoS Protection floods; layers 3 and 4; default infrastructure protection, paid Network or IP Protection
Azure Firewall managed central firewall; network and application rules, FQDN, threat intelligence; Premium TLS inspection and IDPS
WAF layer 7 web attacks (SQL injection, XSS); on Application Gateway, Front Door, CDN
VNet, subnets, NSGs segmentation; NSG rules by priority, source, destination, port, protocol, action
Bastion and Key Vault RDP and SSH without public IP; secrets, keys, certificates, HSM-backed, managed identities
